thread.title_full: Trump signs Iran deal at dinner table in Versailles after months of negotiations - NewsBreak

author: Alana Loftus
title: Trump signs Iran deal at dinner table in Versailles after months of negotiations - NewsBreak
text:
By Alana Loftus ,
53 minutes ago President Donald Trump signed the long-awaited peace agreement with Iran on Wednesday, during a ceremony held at the Palace of Versailles.
The landmark deal was sealed at a dinner hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron inside the iconic palace.
The agreement officially brings to a close the months-long standoff between Washington and Tehran. Following a prolonged period of negotiations and numerous pledges of a settlement, Trump announced earlier this week that a deal had been drawn up. The landmark agreement comes after host Jimmy Kimmel jokingly predicted the president will 'burn down White House' with his Freedom 250 fireworks show .

The White House confirmed that the U.S. president had signed the memorandum of understanding to end the war with Iran. It was confirmed that the agreement is now officially in effect, kicking off the extendable 60-day period for the U.S. and Iran to finalize a comprehensive deal.
Trump signed the document in the presence of Macron and several other high-profile figures. As he completed his signature, someone in the room exclaimed, "Bravo," triggering a round of applause, reports the Express US .
Secretary of State Marco Rubio was nearby, taking the memo away after Trump finished signing.
On Sunday, Vice President JD Vance and Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf both digitally signed the memorandum, which was overseen by Trump, a White House official confirmed.
A BBC report noted that Trump departed the Palace of Versailles just after midnight, following a nearly two-hour dinner. As he made his exit, Trump told reporters, "It's signed. Signed in Versailles. Just signed it."
Following the announcement of a breakthrough agreement earlier this week, both Trump and Iranian officials indicated that a formal signing ceremony would occur sometime this week, later suggesting Friday in Geneva as a possible date.
It's uncertain whether this arrangement will proceed now that the document has been signed by both sides. On Wednesday evening, Trump departed Europe and returned to the U.S..
The peace deal has dominated conversations at this week's G7 summit. Trump has engaged with several key allies, some of whom have publicly expressed reservations about the Iran conflict.
Before Wednesday's dinner at the historic French palace, Trump boasted about Macron's invitation, saying, "And then the French president, who happens to be a very nice man, invited me to dinner at Versailles."
Macron walked a careful line between criticizing the U.S. military strikes on Iran during the confrontation and holding Iran accountable for initiating the hostilities. At the summit, Macron endorsed Trump's peace agreement, saying, "This is an agreement we support."

The landmark deal was sealed at a dinner hosted by French President Emmanuel Macron inside the iconic palace. The landmark agreement comes after host Jimmy Kimmel jokingly predicted the president will 'burn down White House' with his Freedom 250 fireworks show .
